content:
Yesterday we saw that the ordinary manna could not be stored. It had to be gathered fresh every morning, and when it was kept against Yahweh's command it bred worms and gave off a terrible smell. We ended with a question. Out of all the manna that fell in the wilderness, there was one portion that Yahweh commanded to be kept, and that portion never spoiled at all.

Why did it not decay? And what is Yahweh showing us in that preserved omer of bread? Today we find the answer, and it is glorious.

Exodus 16:32-33 tells us that an omer of manna was to be kept for future generations, so that they could see the bread with which Yahweh had fed Israel in the wilderness. Aaron was to place it before Yahweh, and it was to be kept as a testimony. This is very wonderful. All the ordinary manna passed away, but one portion was set apart to remain in the presence of Yahweh. Here we see a beautiful picture of the little flock, the Church, chosen out from among mankind and set apart for a special place before Yahweh. All Israel ate manna in the wilderness, but the preserved portion was different. It was kept before Yahweh, and it did not decay.

Revelation 2:17 says, "To everyone who is victorious I will give some of the manna that has been hidden away". This hidden manna points to a special reward for the overcomers. It is not merely daily food for the wilderness journey. It is a preserved portion, hidden with Yahweh, connected with a life that does not perish. Paul says that "our dying bodies must be transformed into bodies that will never die," and that "this mortal body must be transformed into an immortal body" (1 Corinthians 15:53). This is the hope of the faithful.

The daily manna fed Israel for a single day, but the hidden manna points to a life that can never decay.

Hebrews 9:4 tells us that this manna was kept in a golden jar, and every detail here is meaningful. One omer was each person's daily portion in Exodus 16:16. It was a complete measure; no more and no less. In picture, this preserved omer may show the complete and fixed company whom Yahweh has chosen for the heavenly calling. Revelation 14:1 shows the Lamb standing with the 144,000, having the Father's name written on their foreheads. Ephesians 4:4 says there is one body. Ephesians 1:4 says that Yahweh chose this class in Christ before the foundation of the world. The omer was a complete measure, and the Church also is a complete body, fully known and prepared by Yahweh.

And the jar was gold. In the Tabernacle, gold is connected with the divine nature and with heavenly glory. So here we see corruptible manna placed into an incorruptible golden vessel; a beautiful picture. It points to the Church being made partakers of the divine nature, as Peter says in 2 Peter 1:4. Paul also tells us that the body is sown in corruption but raised in incorruption, sown in weakness but raised in power, sown a natural body but raised a spiritual body (1 Corinthians 15:42-44). The manna that would have rotted on the ground was placed in gold, and there it remained.

The preserved manna did not spoil. Every ordinary portion kept wrongly overnight bred worms, yet this portion remained fresh, because Yahweh Himself commanded it to be preserved. This is a picture of immortality. Immortality is life that cannot decay, cannot diminish, and cannot die.

Christ said that those counted worthy of that resurrection "will never die again" (Luke 20:36). Peter speaks of an inheritance that is kept in heaven, pure and undefiled, beyond the reach of change and decay (1 Peter 1:4). What Yahweh preserves, no time can corrupt. What He places in His presence, no worm can touch. What He glorifies, death cannot destroy.

Notice also where the golden jar was placed. Exodus 16:34 says Aaron placed it before the tablets of the covenant law, so that it could be preserved, and Hebrews 9:4 connects the golden jar of manna with the Ark of the Covenant. The Ark stood in the Most Holy Place, which points to heaven itself, the immediate presence of Yahweh. Hebrews 9:24 says that Christ entered into heaven itself, now to appear before God for us. Therefore the preserved manna placed with the Ark shows us something far greater than an ordinary blessing. It shows the glorified Church placed in Christ, hidden with him in the divine presence. Colossians 3:3 says, "Your real life is hidden with Christ in God". And Christ promised, "When everything is ready, I will come and get you, so that you will always be with me where I am" (John 14:3).

In the Ark there were also Aaron's rod that budded and the tablets of the covenant. Aaron's rod speaks of resurrection and priesthood, because a dead rod brought forth living buds. The tablets speak of the righteousness of Yahweh's covenant & the Church as Judges. And the manna speaks of the preserved life and hidden reward of the faithful. Together, these three things give us a complete picture of the royal priesthood united with its Head, Christ, reigning as Kings, Priests and Judges. Everything in that sacred chest was pointing forward.

The manna was also preserved as a testimony for future generations. Exodus 16:32 says it was kept so that those who came later could see the bread Yahweh gave Israel in the wilderness. The preserved manna was a witness. It testified that Yahweh had fed His people day after day in a place where food could not naturally be found. And so also, the glorified Church will stand as Yahweh's testimony through the coming ages. Ephesians 2:7 says that in the ages to come, Yahweh will show the exceeding riches of His grace and kindness toward us through Christ. The Church will be a living proof of Yahweh's grace, showing what He can do with those who were once weak, earthly, and mortal. Paul said, "You are a letter from Christ, written not with pen and ink, but with the Spirit of the living God" (2 Corinthians 3:3). The faithful Bride will be a living letter of the wilderness journey, testifying that Yahweh can take dust and prepare it for glory, that He can feed His people through every desert day, and that He honours those who honour Him.

What a complete picture we see in the manna. First, there is the daily gathering of the humble believer. Every morning the manna must be gathered fresh. Every day the soul must be fed from Yahweh's Word. If it is neglected, the heart begins to drift. If truth is mishandled, it becomes corruption. But if it is received with obedience, it becomes life. Then we see the preserved portion. One omer was placed in a golden jar and kept before Yahweh, and it did not decay.

It remained as a lasting testimony. In this we see the hope of the faithful Church; chosen, measured, preserved, glorified, hidden with Christ, made partakers of the divine nature, and kept as a testimony of Yahweh's grace in the ages to come. May we gather faithfully each morning now, that we may be found in that preserved portion then. May we never live on yesterday's manna alone. May we not allow truth to decay in our hands through neglect, pride, or disobedience. Let us receive the Word fresh each day, obey it with humility, and keep walking until the wilderness is over and the hidden manna is given to the overcomers.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God,

We thank You that what You preserve, no time can corrupt, and no worm can touch.

You took a portion that would have decayed and kept it fresh in a golden jar before Your face.

Do the same with us; take our weak and mortal lives and hide them with Christ in Your presence.

Make us faithful gatherers now, that we may be found among the preserved portion then.

And let us stand in the ages to come as a living testimony of Your grace.

"He has given us his very great and precious promises, so that you may share his divine nature." - 2 Peter 1:4

In the name of Christ, in whom our life is hidden, we pray. Amen.
